items.title:
Anthropic shares rose 11.0% to close at $91.88 on Friday, their best day since the company's debut last week.
The stock is back above its $83 IPO price, valuing Anthropic at about $1.2 trillion.
items.title_ja:
アンスロピック株は金曜日、11.0％上昇して91.88ドルで取引を終え、先週の同社のデビュー以来最高の日となった。
株価はIPO価格の83ドルを上回り、アンスロピックの評価額は約1兆2000億ドルとなっている。

items.title:
Verizon is in talks to buy fiber provider Fidium at a value of about $6 billion including debt, the FT reports.
Searchlight Capital and Canada's BCI took Fidium, then Consolidated Communications, private at $3.1 billion including debt. A deal may come within weeks.
items.title_ja:
FT紙の報道によると、ベライゾンは光ファイバープロバイダーのフィジウムを負債を含め約60億ドルで買収する交渉を行っているという。
サーチライト・キャピタルとカナダのBCIは、当時コンソリデーテッド・コミュニケーションズだったフィディウムを負債を含む31億ドルで非公開化した。数週間以内に合意が得られる可能性がある。

items.title:
Kazakh banks have raised $1.5 billion to fund a private takeover of gold miner Altynalmas, Reuters reports.
Kazakhstan's government encouraged local banks to finance the deal, Bloomberg reported earlier.
items.title_ja:
ロイター通信によると、カザフスタンの銀行は金鉱会社アルティナルマスの非公開買収に資金を提供するために15億ドルを調達した。
ブルームバーグは先に、カザフスタン政府が地元銀行にこの取引への資金提供を奨励したと報じた。

items.title:
Hong Kong's stock exchange has decided to cancel the listing of China Evergrande New Energy Vehicle, Evergrande's EV unit, with its last trading day set for December 11.
The company says it is considering asking the exchange's review committee to reconsider.
items.title_ja:
香港証券取引所は、恒大のEV部門である中国恒大新能源車の上場を取り消し、最終取引日を12月11日に設定することを決定した。
同社は取引所の審査委員会に再考を求めることを検討しているとしている。

items.title:
An Indian court has allowed Tata Sons' November 30 board meeting on its listing to go ahead, turning down the Tata Trusts' bid to block it, Reuters reports.
The judge said any decisions taken at the meeting will be subject to court order.
items.title_ja:
ロイター通信によると、インドの裁判所はタタ・サンズの上場阻止を求めるタタ・トラストの提案を却下し、タタ・サンズの11月30日の取締役会の開催を許可した。
裁判官は、この会議で下されたいかなる決定も裁判所命令の対象となると述べた。

items.title:
Natixis Investment Managers is weighing a sale of AEW, its US real estate investment manager, Bloomberg reports.
No price for the business has been reported.
items.title_ja:
ブルームバーグによると、ナティクシス・インベストメント・マネージャーズは米国の不動産投資マネージャーであるAEWの売却を検討しているという。
事業価格は報告されていない。

items.title:
AI data center developer LIAN Group has picked London for a potential IPO next year that could raise about $500 million, Bloomberg reports.
The listing would be a boost for London's lackluster market for new share sales.
items.title_ja:
ブルームバーグの報道によると、AIデータセンター開発会社リアン・グループは、来年のIPOの候補地としてロンドンを選択し、約5億ドルを調達できる可能性があるとのこと。
上場は精彩を欠くロンドンの新株販売市場にとって追い風となるだろう。

items.title:
Tata Sons' board will consider the Reserve Bank of India's requirement that it list its shares at a November 30 meeting, the company's lawyer told an Indian court, per Reuters.
The Tata Trusts, which control Tata Sons, are seeking to block or defer that meeting.
items.title_ja:
ロイター通信によると、タタ・サンズの弁護士はインドの法廷で、タタ・サンズの取締役会は11月30日の会合で株式を上場するというインド準備銀行の要求を検討すると述べた。
タタ・サンズを管理するタタ・トラストは、その会合を阻止または延期しようとしている。

items.title:
Portuguese insurer Fidelidade is aiming for an IPO in Lisbon from the second half of 2027, Bloomberg reports, citing people familiar with the matter.
Founded in 1835, Fidelidade is Portugal's largest insurer.
items.title_ja:
ポルトガルの保険会社フィデリダーデは、2027年下半期からリスボンでのIPOを目指しているとブルームバーグが関係者の話として報じた。
1835 年に設立されたフィデリダーデは、ポルトガル最大の保険会社です。

items.title:
Johannesburg's stock exchange is working with Dangote Group toward a possible secondary listing of the Dangote oil refinery in South Africa, Bloomberg reports.
The refinery, Africa's biggest IPO, is set to start trading on the Nigerian Exchange on December 1.
items.title_ja:
ヨハネスブルグ証券取引所は、南アフリカのダンゴテ製油所の二次上場の可能性に向けてダンゴテ・グループと協力しているとブルームバーグが報じた。
アフリカ最大のIPOであるこの製油所は、12月1日にナイジェリア取引所で取引を開始する予定だ。

items.title:
Kenya Airways plans to raise $1.5 billion from a strategic investor by the middle of 2027, its chairman said, Reuters reports.
The deal will mix equity and debt. The carrier begins sharing details with potential investors today, and other airlines could be among them.
items.title_ja:
ロイター通信の報道によると、ケニア航空は2027年半ばまでに戦略的投資家から15億ドルを調達する計画であると会長が述べた。
この取引では株式と負債が混在することになる。同社は本日、潜在的な投資家と詳細を共有し始めており、他の航空会社もその中に含まれる可能性がある。

items.title:
Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund has dropped plans to take medical supplies distributor NUPCO public in an IPO that could have raised close to $1 billion, Semafor reports.
The decision is tied to internal matters at NUPCO, not the regional war, people familiar said.
items.title_ja:
サウジアラビアの公的投資基金は、10億ドル近くを調達できた可能性のある医療用品販売業者NUPCOのIPO計画を撤回したとセマフォーが報じた。
関係者らによると、この決定は地域戦争ではなく、NUPCOの内部問題に関係しているという。

items.title:
Tesla has filed plans with Germany's Federal Cartel Office to acquire EMAG, a German machine tool maker, according to the antitrust regulator.
Terms of the deal were not disclosed.
items.title_ja:
独禁規制当局によると、テスラはドイツの工作機械メーカーＥＭＡＧを買収する計画をドイツ連邦カルテル庁に提出した。
契約条件は明らかにされていない。

items.title:
German drone maker Quantum Systems is moving toward an IPO as sales to Ukraine and the German military jump, Bloomberg reports.
The defense startup is valued at about €7 billion, the Financial Times has reported.
items.title_ja:
ドイツのドローンメーカー、クアンタム・システムズは、ウクライナとドイツ軍への売り上げが急増する中、IPOに向けて動いているとブルームバーグが報じた。
フィナンシャル・タイムズ紙の報道によると、この防衛関連スタートアップの評価額は約70億ユーロだという。

Even Tesla can't get enough TSMC capacity.
According to Taiwanese media, Tesla's next generation AI5 chip will go to Optimus robots and data centers FIRST, while its cars stay on AI4 and an updated AI4.5.
The reason is TSMC's 3nm capacity. Global Unichip, Tesla's custom chip design partner for AI5, got a much bigger 3nm allocation for 2027, but it still can't cover every big customer.
Supply chain sources say Global Unichip will give priority to data center projects from Google and Microsoft, including Google's Axion server chips. That leaves less room for Tesla.
AI5 isn't expected to go into cars at scale until 2028, when more 3nm capacity comes online.
This is the AI infrastructure story in one picture. Hyperscalers are taking the leading edge capacity, and everyone else, even $TSLA, has to wait in line. That's pricing POWER for $TSM.
Milk Road AI (@MilkRoadAI)
Microsoft and Google are turning to Intel's EMIB packaging because they cannot get enough TSMC CoWoS capacity.
On November 18, Intel and Microsoft said Microsoft will use Intel Foundry's EMIB technology for its own Azure chips, becoming the first company to publicly confirm that.
Google is reportedly using EMIB for future TPU versions designed with MediaTek.
Reports put EMIB-T substrate yields at around 35% last quarter, short of a 50% target by year end but the move still tells you how tight advanced packaging is.
When the biggest buyers in the world start looking for a second source, that is a demand signal, not a weakness.
We think this is another reminder that the bottleneck in AI is not just the wafers but the packaging that ties the chips together.

サプライチェーン関係者によると、グローバル・ユニチップはグーグルのアクシオン・サーバー・チップを含むグーグルとマイクロソフトのデータセンター・プロジェクトを優先するという。そうなるとテスラの余地は少なくなる。
AI5 が自動車に大規模に搭載されるのは、より多くの 3nm 容量が登場する 2028 年になると予想されています。
これは、AI インフラストラクチャの物語を 1 枚の絵で表したものです。ハイパースケーラーが最先端のキャパシティを占有しており、$TSLA を含む他の企業は列に並んで待たなければなりません。それは、$TSM で POWER を価格設定することです。
ミルクロードAI (@MilkRoadAI)
Microsoft と Google は、十分な TSMC CoWoS 容量を確保できないため、Intel の EMIB パッケージに注目しています。
11月18日、IntelとMicrosoftは、Microsoftが自社のAzureチップにIntel FoundryのEMIB技術を使用する予定であると発表し、それを公に認めた最初の企業となった。
Google は、MediaTek で設計された将来の TPU バージョンに EMIB を使用していると伝えられています。
レポートによると、前四半期のEMIB-T基板の歩留まりは約35%で、年末までの目標である50%には達していませんが、この動きは依然として先進的なパッケージングがいかに厳しいかを物語っています。

Elon Musk tried to buy his way to the front of the memory line, and Samsung basically told him to get in line.

So Musk went further and offered to guarantee financing for a brand new Samsung chip plant. Even that reportedly wasn't enough to give him an edge.

The stock fell about 20% on Wednesday after the guide.
So Wall Street is selling memory stocks on oversupply fears, while their customers are cutting guidance because they cannot get enough memory.

Starlink Mobile connects regular phones directly to satellites, and SpaceX is scaling that service fast.

The plan is to process data in space and send it back to Earth over laser links into the Starlink network, with radio links only for backup command and control.
This is a conditional license with a long runway and SpaceX has until November 2033 to get a single satellite operating, until 2035 to deploy 100,000, until 2038 for 500,000, and until 2040 for the full million.

On market crashes like today, I'm reminded of a piece of advice I got from a CIO mentor that traded during the dotcom and 08 crashes and lived to tell the tale.
He said: "Treat investing the same way you treat life."
That's all. It has stuck with me for many years because after filling in the blanks, you're forced to become "better" in both portfolio management and life management. It's uncanny how correlated they are.
Strip either one down and you're left with the same raw materials: time and uncertainty.
Every investment gives up something certain today for something uncertain tomorrow. So does nearly everything that matters in life. Love, learning, raising a child, starting a new job. Anything.
Both reward patience, but only after testing it.
You can't generate performance without risking losses, the same way you can't love without risking grief.
But fundamentally, the first rule of portfolio and life management is survival.
You can come back from most losses, but not from the one that takes you out of the game.
It's always darkest before the dawn.

Memory name buybacks + pricing projections:
- $SKHY doubled its daily buybacks from ~$290M -> $581M, after Korea relaxed its buyback rules, explicitly citing "undervaluation"
- $MU Dec 9, 2026 marks the end of the first 2 under initial CHIPS act agreements (where there was restrictions on buybacks).
Micron stated it expects to return 100% of excess cash to shareholders, and that they'll increase returns past Dec 9th.
On the supply/pricing side per Trendforce:
- Conventional DRAM contract price increases are expected to narrow throughout 2027, with prices potentially leveling off in the H2 2027 before declining in 2028
Under the assumptions that:
--- Consumer electronics manufacturers are facing mounting sales pressure
--- Chinese CSPs scaling back DRAM demand in early 4Q26 (but absorbed by US CSPs)
--- markets expect a cautious policy stance toward domestic DC development
--- $NVDA scales back its financing support for neocloud providers.
They forecast conventional DRAM to increase 10%-15% Q4 2026, with further increases up 3%-8% Q1 2027.
In another bear case they give:
--- server OEMs will further scale back procurement following downward revisions to demand
--- widespread inventory reductions across the supply chain
--- downside risks include reduced investment and potential consolidation among neocloud providers
"overall server shipment growth could begin decelerating as early as 2027, causing conventional DRAM contract prices to reverse course and begin declining in 4Q27, with price declines widening in 2028."
___
$MU CEO said earlier: "we expect memory and storage supply demand conditions to be much tighter in 2027 and 2028 than they were in 2026"...
But I think everyone is starting to price in a 2028 demand/pricing destruction already (which hasn't happened). Also I do think a lot of new price floor LTAs should change how we look at memory name durability.
As long as durability and pricing remains elevated for longer periods of time, which $SKHY likely has more information to, I'd agree with them shares look increasingly undervalued.

SOME PERSONAL THOUGHTS AHEAD OF WEEKEND
I wanted to share a few thoughts heading into the weekend because at least for me this has been one of most mentally exhausting stretches I've experienced investing in growth stocks.
And honestly one of the things I've found most difficult has very little to do with market itself since it's how much mental real estate I apparently occupy in the minds of certain "gurus" on this platform whom I've never met, followed or even spoken to.
I started sharing my thoughts on X back in 2023 simply because I genuinely love investing and wanted somewhere to talk about market, share my research and connect with people who enjoyed it as much as I did and I never imagined that would turn into an account reaching 100 million impressions every month or that I'd eventually find myself appearing on national television every week.
I'm incredibly grateful because this platform accelerated my career at a relatively young age and opened doors that otherwise might have taken me many more years to reach but I'd be lying if I said spotlight wasn't intense since the larger my audience becomes and more visible I am the more I've realized that success also seems to attract resentment from people I've never interacted with or affected in any way possible.
Daniel has a phrase for this that I think captures it perfectly because "hating up" is absolutely real especially online where people seem more comfortable attacking someone who has become visible than examining why that person's success bothers them in the first place.
Like I've had people accuse me of taking an investment idea from them despite fact that I don't follow them and have never even seen their work while others take a disagreement over a particular thesis and turn it into a personal judgment about whether I know anything about investing.
What I find especially strange is that some of these individuals are in their 40s and 50s have been doing this for decades and still seem determined to tear down a 33 year old who is simply willing to publish his research, explain what he believes and put his own money behind those convictions (I've never asked anyone to agree with me or suggested that my way of investing is the only way to succeed).
And I think that last part is important because I do all of this under my real name and face, publicly disclose what I own through my subs service, share my position sizes and actual dollars I've invested and expose myself to scrutiny over every good decision and every mistake along the way.
There's absolutely nothing wrong with choosing to remain anonymous and I respect anyone who prefers to operate that way but theres just a different level of personal accountability when people know exactly who you are and watch you explain your thesis on camera and follow your positions in real time and wait for first opportunity to use a bad outcome against you... just remember being wrong privately costs you money but being wrong publicly can also cost you reputation, confidence and peace of mind which is something I don't think people fully appreciate until they've experienced it themselves.
None of this is to suggest that criticism should be off limits because disagreement is a huge part of investing but what I truly struggle to understand is why disagreement so often has to become personal... especially during periods like this when so many people are already dealing with painful drawdowns and questioning decisions they made with the best information available to them.
Markets eventually humble every single one of us regardless of how experienced we are or how much success we've had and anyone who stays in this long enough will eventually experience a thesis that breaks or a position they sized too aggressively or a drawdown that exposes a weakness in their process or a decision they wish they could take back so that's why I think showing people grace matters so much because you never know when you'll find yourself on the other side of that experience hoping others will extend you the same understanding.
And also just remember it cost absolutely nothing to root for people, respect the work they're putting in and recognize that someone can be wrong about an investment without deserving to be ridiculed for it and I genuinely wish more people on this platform understood that being publicly wrong doesn't erase courage it takes to stand behind your own convictions in the first place.
And to the people who've made rooting against me a hobby I genuinely hope you find the same energy for your own work that you've found for mine because if you're spending more time waiting for someone else to fail than building something of your own then maybe my portfolio isn't what needs your attention.
I'll be here next week, same name, same face, same conviction.
items.title_ja:
週末に向けての個人的な考え
少なくとも私にとって、これは成長株への投資で経験した中で最も精神的に疲れる作業の1つだったので、週末に向けていくつかの考えを共有したいと思いました。
そして正直に言うと、私が最も難しいと感じたことの1つは、市場自体とはほとんど関係がありません。それは、私が会ったことも、フォローしたことも、話したことさえない、このプラットフォーム上の特定の「達人」の心の中で私がどれだけの精神的領域を占めていると思われるかということだからです。
私が X についての考えを 2023 年に共有し始めたのは、単純に投資が心から好きで、市場について話したり、自分の研究を共有したり、同じように市場を楽しんでいる人々とつながる場所が欲しかったからです。それが毎月 1 億インプレッションに達するアカウントに成長したり、最終的には全国放送のテレビに毎週出演するようになるとは想像もしていませんでした。
このプラットフォームのおかげで、比較的若い年齢で私のキャリアが加速し、到達するまでにさらに何年もかかっていた可能性がある扉が開かれたので、非常に感謝しています。しかし、視聴者が増えて知名度が上がるほど、成功は、私がこれまで交流したことのない、あるいは何らかの影響を与えたことのない人たちからの怒りを引き寄せるようにも見えることに気づいたので、スポットライトが強くなかったと言ったら嘘になります。
ダニエルはこれについてのフレーズを持っていますが、これはそれを完璧に捉えていると思います。なぜなら、「憎しみ」は絶対に現実のもので、特にオンラインでは、人々は誰かを調べるよりも、目立つようになった人を攻撃する方が安心しているようです。

Beakdown of off balance sheet commitments versus on balance sheet liabilities:
• $GOOGL $1.1T / $113B
• $META $810B / $110B
• $MSFT $575B / $110B
• $NVDA $422B / $37B
• $AMZN $419B / $223B
• $ORCL $322B / $157B
Important to call out that a lot of this spending is already contractually committed meaning even if AI CapEx growth starts slowing that the demand for power, cooling and networking doesn't just disappear overnight but there is a real question of how comfortable these companies will be to fund those commitments as credit markets become more cautious.

CHRIS CAMILLO SAYS NVIDIA $NVDA HAS BECOME A LEVERED BET ON THE AI NARRATIVE
@ChrisCamillo says he didn't buy the selloff while Jensen Huang was gone, because he had no idea how long he'd be out.
"Jensen was way more than a person to that company"
Camillo says Huang personally holds Nvidia's ecosystem together through deals and relationships with partners and competitors, tying the company to every part of AI.
"If the AI trade wins, Nvidia wins"
The flip side, he says, is that if the AI narrative falls apart, it's terrible news for Nvidia. His question for investors is whether demand for compute will be near endless over the next few years. If you don't think so, he says Nvidia isn't a company you want to be in.

items.title:
NVIDIA $NVDA BLACKWELL CHIPS REPORTEDLY TURNED UP IN A SHANGHAI DATA CENTER LINKED TO ALICE HUANG
Jensen Huang once claimed these racks were too big to smuggle. A single GB300 NVL72 rack can weigh more than 3,300 pounds, about the size of a giant fridge.
Two Chinese firms listed Blackwell hardware at the site in filings with Chinese regulators and lenders, per Bloomberg:
- Shanghai Shuoyao put up a GB300 NVL72 rack, among Nvidia's most powerful products, as collateral for a 96M yuan ($14M) loan
- Shanghai Kezhan described a GB200 server at the site when it took a 90M yuan loan from a firm owned by a Shanghai government agency
- The rack's serial number matched a Gigabyte-built unit in a public warranty database
Blackwell chips have always needed a US license to ship to China. It's unclear how the rack got there.
The site has ties to Megaspeed, the company Alice Huang founded in 2023, which is under US investigation and was added to a US trade blacklist this month. Megaspeed denies wrongdoing, and Bloomberg says it has no evidence Megaspeed itself sent hardware to the site.
Nvidia didn't respond to Bloomberg's questions. Gigabyte says it follows all applicable laws.

items.title:
QUANTUM COMPUTERS HAVE A HUGE WASTE PROBLEM, AND INFLEQTION SAYS IT CUT IT DOWN DRAMATICALLY
Quantum computers make a lot of errors. To get one reliable unit of computing power, called a logical qubit, you have to bundle together many error-prone ones, called physical qubits, as backup.
The industry used to think that each reliable qubit could take 1,000 to 10,000 backups.
Infleqtion says it needs about 2.6.
It built 30 reliable qubits out of just 80 physical ones, using individual atoms held inside a chamber.
Your phone does something similar on Wi-Fi. To send you a 1 MB photo, it moves about 1.5 MB of data, with the extra there to catch errors. Infleqtion says its quantum computer now works closer to that than to what anyone expected.
The company says 100 reliable qubits is the point where quantum computers become commercially useful. Wasting fewer qubits gets it there much sooner.

業界では、信頼できる量子ビットごとに 1,000 ～ 10,000 回のバックアップが必要だと考えられていました。
Infleqtion では約 2.6 が必要です。
チャンバー内に保持された個々の原子を使用して、わずか 80 個の物理量子ビットから 30 個の信頼できる量子ビットを構築しました。
携帯電話は Wi-Fi 上で同様のことを行います。 1 MB の写真を送信するには、約 1.5 MB のデータが移動され、残りのデータはエラーを検出するために使用されます。 Infleqtion 社は、同社の量子コンピューターは現在、誰もが予想していたよりもそれに近い状態で動作すると述べています。
同社は、量子コンピューターが商業的に有用になるポイントは信頼性の高い 100 量子ビットであると述べています。無駄な量子ビットが減れば、より早くそこに到達します。

Hackers have breached the US Air Force's flagship Cloud One computing platform, per Reuters.
Cloud One runs everything from pay and logistics to air defense radar feeds across North America and munitions tracking at more than 200 sites. One source says the intruders reached the system's "control plane."
items.title_ja:
ロイター通信によると、ハッカーが米空軍の主力コンピューティングプラットフォーム「Cloud One」に侵入した。
Cloud One は、給与や物流から、北米全土の防空レーダー フィードや 200 以上の拠点での軍需品の追跡に至るまで、あらゆるものを運営しています。ある情報筋によると、侵入者はシステムの「コントロールプレーン」に到達したという。

items.title:
Canada’s job growth since 2019 has come mostly from the public sector, per Build Canada.
The public sector employed about 1 in 5 Canadians in 2019, but has accounted for 42% of jobs added since, the third-highest rate in the G7.
items.title_ja:
ビルド・カナダによると、2019年以降のカナダの雇用の増加は主に公共部門によるものだという。
公共部門は2019年にカナダ人の約5人に1人を雇用したが、それ以降追加された雇用の42％を占めており、G7の中で3番目に高い割合となっている。

items.title:
Gen X feels worse about the economy than Gen Z and millennials, per Fortune.
Gen X’s consumer confidence has averaged about 60 over the past six months, near a five-year low, per the Conference Board. Gen Z and millennials have held steady at around 100 and 90.
items.title_ja:
フォーチュン誌によると、X世代はZ世代やミレニアル世代よりも経済について悪く感じているという。
コンファレンス・ボードによると、X世代の消費者信頼感は過去6か月で平均約60で、ここ5年で最低水準に近い水準となっている。 Z世代とミレニアル世代は100歳と90歳前後で安定している。
